subject: Maths
title: Two-step equations
subtitle: Solving Linear Equations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve two-step linear equations by undoing operations in reverse order.

key_vocab.definition: A two-step equation needs TWO inverse operations, e.g. 3x + 4 = 19 → subtract 4, then divide by 3.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve two-step linear equations by undoing operations in reverse order.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: two-step equation -- A two-step equation needs TWO inverse operations, e.g. 3x + 4 = 19 → subtract 4, then divide by 3.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Undo the LAST operation first. For 3x + 4: the last operation done to x was +4, so undo +4 first.
3x + 4 = 19 ⇒ 3x = 15 ⇒ x = 5
−4 then ÷3

Key examples:
  ✓ 3x + 4 = 19  (−4 then ÷3)
  ✓ x = 5 (check: 15+4=19)  (always check)
  ✓ Undo +/− first  (reverse BIDMAS)
  ✗ 3x + 4 = 19 → ÷3 first  (wrong order)
  ✗ Forget to do both sides  (must do BOTH)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – +/×
  Solve 3x + 4 = 19
  Subtract 4 from both sides
  3x = 15
  Divide both sides by 3 → x = 5
  x = 5
  (Check: 3(5) + 4 = 15 + 4 = 19 ✓)

Example 2 – −/×
  Solve 5x − 7 = 18
  Add 7 to both sides
  5x = 25
  Divide by 5 → x = 5
  x = 5
  (Check: 5(5) − 7 = 18 ✓)

sections.title: Division form
sections.content:
x is divided. Undo the +/− first, then multiply.

(a) x ÷ 2 + 3 = 8
(b) x ÷ 4 − 1 = 3
(c) x ÷ 5 + 2 = 7
(d) x ÷ 3 − 2 = 4

sections.title: Fractional answers
sections.content:
Don't be put off by fractions or decimals.

(a) 4x + 3 = 10
(b) 3x − 2 = 8
(c) 5x + 1 = 8
(d) 6x − 5 = 7

sections.title: Mixed two-step
sections.content:
Choose the right order of operations.

(a) 9x + 7 = 70
(b) x ÷ 6 + 4 = 9
(c) 12x − 5 = 31
(d) x ÷ 2 − 7 = −3
(e) 11x + 9 = 86

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✗ 3x + 4 = 19 → first divide by 3
✓ Subtract 4 first, THEN divide
✓ 5x − 7 = 18 means x = 5
✓ Undo BIDMAS in reverse order
✗ x can never be a fraction
